text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own EXCAVA'S OWN interface — visibility, liveliness, clarity, enjoyment, speed of OUR scre

name: Facet
text: Build the Excava interface in Figma as a clickable prototype first. It lets users *feel* the flow before any code exists, exposing UX flaws early when they’re cheap to fix. The trade-off is that this delays the "real speed" proof until we move to live HTML/CSS, but clarity beats speed in early discovery.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Figma’s polished demo still risks users mistaking the prototype for the real interface, hiding real speed gaps until we hit live HTML/CSS. A better alternative is to prototype only the risky flows in low-fidelity wireframes—then measure actual screentime against those flows to settle the argument.
